brief: A tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers, with hooks for small hand tools.

requirements.requirement: Tool rack that hangs on a wall from keyhole hangers
requirements.evidence: One Hex base full piece (piece:0,0,0;full) carries a keyhole hanger (accessory:0#0,0#0, hex-acc-keyhole) on the wall-side face, so it hangs on screws already in a wall. Mesh check reads clear.

Two hook plates (accessory:0#0,0#1 and 0#0,0#2, hex-acc-hook), each carrying two hooks, are bolted to the base: four hooks total. However the configurator only lets a cable coil, gaffer tape or FPV goggles hang on a hook; a screwdriver or pliers cannot be hung on them in the build, so the hooks are placed but hand tools are not shown hanging.

finish.summary: Built a single-cell wall tool rack: a full hex base with a keyhole hanger on one face, two hook plates (four hooks) on adjacent faces, and the remaining open faces capped, with joints locked. Mesh check is clear and no rule errors remain. Caveats: the hooks are oriented by face assignment I could not verify visually, and the configurator's hook accepts only coils, tape or goggles as props, so small hand tools are not shown hanging. Material suitability and load capacity for holding tools are not checked by the configurator.

lines.label: M6 x 20 socket head screw, ISO 4762

notes: Tighten every M6 to 2 N.m: HAND TOOLS ONLY, never a cordless driver. These bolts clamp printed PETG, not metal: at the bolt's own 10.4 N.m rating the head crushes the plastic under it and the joint fails silently, looking tight while holding nothing. Snug, then a nudge. Re-check the bolts after the first few weeks: PETG relaxes under load and the clamp will have eased.
